summary.intent: Run the GSD plan-phase and execute-phase workflows end-to-end for cipher-box phase 68.2 (SDK-owned read chain and resolved folder listings), while also spinning up a parallel git worktree to start independent phase 69 (Rust FUSE/WinFsp) work.
summary.outcome: Phase 68.2 was fully planned (12 plans/7 waves, plan-checker PASSED) and executed (62 commits, all waves green), but final phase verification found the headline SC#5 desync bug was not actually fixed — `ensureFolderLoaded` still short-circuits on cached entries — so the phase was left in gaps_found (4/5) status and gap-closure planning was kicked off; a separate worktree for phase 69 was created off origin/main but planning/execution there was not started.

repo: cipher-box is a pnpm monorepo where worktree-based parallel execution is expensive (each worktree needs its own pnpm install) and not worth it when most waves are single-plan — sequential execution on the main tree was chosen instead for phase 68.2, reusing already-installed node_modules.

GSD requirement checkboxes (SDK-READ-01/02/04 style) get marked `[x]` prematurely by early-wave executors even when the acceptance criteria depend on later-wave deletions; this must be caught and reverted to `[ ]` until the real completing plan lands, then re-marked.

The D-07 'no raw IPFS/IPNS access anywhere in apps/web/src' boundary, when taken literally, sweeps in off-path pockets (BYO-pinning config-blob resolve/publish, auth-bootstrap/device-registry crypto) not mentioned in the folder-listing success criteria — this needed an explicit scope decision (AskUserQuestion) rather than being left ambiguous for the planner.

Planner coverage for a phase like this consistently underestimates the true importer graph of modules slated for deletion — the residual importer set for Plan 11's 4 deleted services grew from ~5 flagged components to 8-9 actual files (utils/fileTypes.ts, lib/crypto/key-wrapping.ts, vault-settings.store.ts, TextEditorDialog.tsx, useStreamingPreview.ts, download.service.ts, etc.) discovered only via targeted grep audits before dispatch.
Web-side plans in this monorepo must rebuild the SDK dist before their own typecheck runs, otherwise cross-package staleness silently masks real type errors.

gsd-tools query commit helper has a known false-negative: it can report `commit_failed` even when `git log` confirms the commit landed cleanly — always verify with git log rather than trusting the reported status.

code.finding: ensureFolderLoaded short-circuits on cached folderTree entries and never re-resolves the folder's IPNS on repeat navigation — root cause of the unclosed SC#5 owner/grantee desync bug; listFolder's freshness check compares folder.sequenceNumber against itself, a self-referential no-op.
enforceResolved (ROT-07 anti-rollback gate) wired into the root folder resolve path as part of plan 68.2-01.
enforceResolved gate also wired into dfsFindFolder's child loop (plan 68.2-01), alongside the pre-existing write-path gate at line 1156.

resolveChildren docstring documents intentional graceful degradation: unverifiable sibling children are skipped rather than failing the whole listing, because the target folder is already gated before this runs — confirmed not to swallow the ROT-07 security guarantee.

workflow: For security-critical or deviation-flagged executor output, independently re-run the actual acceptance tests/gates rather than trusting the subagent's self-reported PASS — this caught nothing wrong in 68.2 but was the correct discipline (e.g. re-running the ROT-07 gate test and the D-07 grep gate directly).

When creating a worktree for parallel independent work, use plain `git worktree add` (not EnterWorktree) if you need to remain in the current checkout driving other work; base it on the last-known origin/main ref if `git fetch` is unavailable in a sandboxed session, and verify the fetched ref is still current before treating it as a clean base.

ScheduleWakeup delaySeconds must be computed from a freshly-fetched current timestamp, not one captured before an interruption (e.g. hitting a quota/session limit) — reusing a stale timestamp produced a wake scheduled ~25 minutes later than intended.
A stray/duplicate ScheduleWakeup that can't be cleanly retracted is generally harmless if the resumed work will recognize it already completed and treat the redundant firing as a no-op.

friction: Hit the session/quota limit mid-execution (reset at 4am Europe/Berlin), interrupting Wave 4 between plans 04 and 06.

First ScheduleWakeup attempt used a delay computed off a pre-interruption timestamp, resulting in a wake time 25 minutes later than intended (04:35 instead of 04:10) — had to detect and recompute against the real current time.
Could not cleanly retract the earlier, now-redundant scheduled wakeup once the user said to just keep going.
`git fetch` failed with no network access from the sandboxed session, requiring reliance on the last-known local `origin/main` ref plus manual verification that it was still current.
A grep command for mapping deletion-blocking importers failed due to zsh glob syntax and had to be rewritten.
The post-planning gap-analysis gate's JSON output contained control characters that broke the parser, requiring the check to be re-run directly instead.
open_items: SC#5 desync bug (SDK-READ-03) is unresolved — gap-closure planning (`/gsd-plan-phase 68.2 --gaps`) was just kicked off to design a live-resolve-on-navigation path through the ROT-07 gate, distinct from the cached write-mutation fast path.
Verifier noted ~14 other web-e2e failures plausibly share the same ensureFolderLoaded staleness root cause — worth checking once the SC#5 fix lands.

Phase 69 worktree (`/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box-phase69`, branch `feat/phase-69-fuse-winfsp`) was created off origin/main but discuss-phase/plan-phase/execute-phase for it have not been started.

Phase 69's design-mirroring dependency on 68.2 (SDK-owned read-chain design mirrored on the Rust side) means its worktree lacks 68.2's CONTEXT/RESEARCH docs — offered but not yet performed: copying that context into the phase-69 worktree.
Phase 69 planning should account for the grant-root scope algorithm (net-new/under-specified per roadmap) and the unresolved FUSE delete-authority-model question (Open Q3) before planning starts.
